```python
  metadata: PodV1Metadata,
  spec: PodV1Spec,

  timeouts: PodV1Timeouts = None

```

##### `put_metadata` <a name="put_metadata" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1.putMetadata"></a>

```python
def put_metadata(
  annotations: typing.Mapping[str] = None,
  generate_name: str = None,
  labels: typing.Mapping[str] = None,
  name: str = None,
  namespace: str = None
) -> None
```

###### `annotations`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="annotations" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1.putMetadata.parameter.annotations"></a>

- *Type:* typing.Mapping[str]

An unstructured key value map stored with the pod that may be used to store arbitrary metadata.

More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/annotations/

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#annotations PodV1#annotations}

---

###### `generate_name`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="generate_name" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1.putMetadata.parameter.generateName"></a>

- *Type:* str

Prefix, used by the server, to generate a unique name ONLY IF the `name` field has not been provided.

This value will also be combined with a unique suffix. More info: https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#idempotency

##### `is_construct` <a name="is_construct" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1.isConstruct"></a>

```python
from cdktn_provider_kubernetes import pod_v1

podV1.PodV1.is_construct(
  x: typing.Any
)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* typing.Any

Any object.


- *Type:* str

Set DNS policy for containers within the pod.

Valid values are 'ClusterFirstWithHostNet', 'ClusterFirst', 'Default' or 'None'. DNS parameters given in DNSConfig will be merged with the policy selected with DNSPolicy. To have DNS options set along with hostNetwork, you have to specify DNS policy explicitly to 'ClusterFirstWithHostNet'. Defaults to 'ClusterFirst'. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/dns-pod-service/#pod-s-dns-policy

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#dns_policy PodV1#dns_policy}

```python

```

- *Type:* bool | cdktn.IResolvable

Share a single process namespace between all of the containers in a pod.

When this is set containers will be able to view and signal processes from other containers in the same pod, and the first process in each container will not be assigned PID 1. HostPID and ShareProcessNamespace cannot both be set. Optional: Defaults to false.

##### `termination_grace_period_seconds`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="termination_grace_period_seconds" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1Spec.property.terminationGracePeriodSeconds"></a>

```python
termination_grace_period_seconds: typing.Union[int, float]
```

- *Type:* typing.Union[int, float]

Optional duration in seconds the pod needs to terminate gracefully.

May be decreased in delete request. Value must be non-negative integer. The value zero indicates delete immediately. If this value is nil, the default grace period will be used instead. The grace period is the duration in seconds after the processes running in the pod are sent a termination signal and the time when the processes are forcibly halted with a kill signal. Set this value longer than the expected cleanup time for your process.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#termination_grace_period_seconds PodV1#termination_grace_period_seconds}

##### `stdin`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="stdin" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecContainer.property.stdin"></a>

```python
stdin: bool | IResolvable
```

- *Type:* bool | cdktn.IResolvable

Whether this container should allocate a buffer for stdin in the container runtime.

If this is not set, reads from stdin in the container will always result in EOF.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#stdin PodV1#stdin}

---

##### `stdin_once`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="stdin_once" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecContainer.property.stdinOnce"></a>

```python
stdin_once: bool | IResolvable
```

- *Type:* bool | cdktn.IResolvable

Whether the container runtime should close the stdin channel after it has been opened by a single attach.

When stdin is true the stdin stream will remain open across multiple attach sessions. If stdinOnce is set to true, stdin is opened on container start, is empty until the first client attaches to stdin, and then remains open and accepts data until the client disconnects, at which time stdin is closed and remains closed until the container is restarted. If this flag is false, a container processes that reads from stdin will never receive an EOF.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#stdin_once PodV1#stdin_once}

---

##### `termination_message_path`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="termination_message_path" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecContainer.property.terminationMessagePath"></a>

```python
termination_message_path: str
```

- *Type:* str

Optional: Path at which the file to which the container's termination message will be written is mounted into the container's filesystem.

Message written is intended to be brief final status, such as an assertion failure message. Defaults to /dev/termination-log. Cannot be updated.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#termination_message_path PodV1#termination_message_path}

---

##### `termination_message_policy`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="termination_message_policy" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecContainer.property.terminationMessagePolicy"></a>

```python
termination_message_policy: str
```

- *Type:* str

Optional: Indicate how the termination message should be populated.

File will use the contents of terminationMessagePath to populate the container status message on both success and failure. FallbackToLogsOnError will use the last chunk of container log output if the termination message file is empty and the container exited with an error. The log output is limited to 2048 bytes or 80 lines, whichever is smaller. Defaults to File. Cannot be updated.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#termination_message_policy PodV1#termination_message_policy}

### PodV1SpecContainerLifecyclePostStartExec <a name="PodV1SpecContainerLifecyclePostStartExec" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecContainerLifecyclePostStartExec"></a>

#### Initializer <a name="Initializer" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecContainerLifecyclePostStartExec.Initializer"></a>

```python
from cdktn_provider_kubernetes import pod_v1

podV1.PodV1SpecContainerLifecyclePostStartExec(
  command: typing.List[str] = None
)
```

#### Properties <a name="Properties" id="Properties"></a>

| **Name** | **Type** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <code><a href="#@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecContainerLifecyclePostStartExec.property.command">command</a></code> | <code>typing.List[str]</code> | Command is the command line to execute inside the container, the working directory for the command is root ('/') in the container's filesystem. |

---

##### `command`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="command" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecContainerLifecyclePostStartExec.property.command"></a>

```python
command: typing.List[str]
```

- *Type:* typing.List[str]

Command is the command line to execute inside the container, the working directory for the command is root ('/') in the container's filesystem.

The command is simply exec'd, it is not run inside a shell, so traditional shell instructions. To use a shell, you need to explicitly call out to that shell. Exit status of 0 is treated as live/healthy and non-zero is unhealthy.

```python
command: typing.List[str]
```

- *Type:* typing.List[str]

Command is the command line to execute inside the container, the working directory for the command is root ('/') in the container's filesystem.

The command is simply exec'd, it is not run inside a shell, so traditional shell instructions. To use a shell, you need to explicitly call out to that shell. Exit status of 0 is treated as live/healthy and non-zero is unhealthy.

Command is the command line to execute inside the container, the working directory for the command is root ('/') in the container's filesystem.

The command is simply exec'd, it is not run inside a shell, so traditional shell instructions. To use a shell, you need to explicitly call out to that shell. Exit status of 0 is treated as live/healthy and non-zero is unhealthy.

##### `run_as_non_root`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="run_as_non_root" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecContainerSecurityContext.property.runAsNonRoot"></a>

```python
run_as_non_root: bool | IResolvable
```

- *Type:* bool | cdktn.IResolvable

Indicates that the container must run as a non-root user.

If true, the Kubelet will validate the image at runtime to ensure that it does not run as UID 0 (root) and fail to start the container if it does. If unset or false, no such validation will be performed. May also be set in PodSecurityContext. If set in both SecurityContext and PodSecurityContext, the value specified in SecurityContext takes precedence.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#run_as_non_root PodV1#run_as_non_root}

```python
run_as_user: str
```

- *Type:* str

The UID to run the entrypoint of the container process.

Defaults to user specified in image metadata if unspecified. May also be set in PodSecurityContext. If set in both SecurityContext and PodSecurityContext, the value specified in SecurityContext takes precedence.


Command is the command line to execute inside the container, the working directory for the command is root ('/') in the container's filesystem.

The command is simply exec'd, it is not run inside a shell, so traditional shell instructions. To use a shell, you need to explicitly call out to that shell. Exit status of 0 is treated as live/healthy and non-zero is unhealthy.

##### `stdin`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="stdin" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecInitContainer.property.stdin"></a>

```python
stdin: bool | IResolvable
```

- *Type:* bool | cdktn.IResolvable

Whether this container should allocate a buffer for stdin in the container runtime.

If this is not set, reads from stdin in the container will always result in EOF.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#stdin PodV1#stdin}

---

##### `stdin_once`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="stdin_once" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecInitContainer.property.stdinOnce"></a>

```python
stdin_once: bool | IResolvable
```

- *Type:* bool | cdktn.IResolvable

Whether the container runtime should close the stdin channel after it has been opened by a single attach.

When stdin is true the stdin stream will remain open across multiple attach sessions. If stdinOnce is set to true, stdin is opened on container start, is empty until the first client attaches to stdin, and then remains open and accepts data until the client disconnects, at which time stdin is closed and remains closed until the container is restarted. If this flag is false, a container processes that reads from stdin will never receive an EOF.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#stdin_once PodV1#stdin_once}

---

##### `termination_message_path`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="termination_message_path" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecInitContainer.property.terminationMessagePath"></a>

```python
termination_message_path: str
```

- *Type:* str

Optional: Path at which the file to which the container's termination message will be written is mounted into the container's filesystem.

Message written is intended to be brief final status, such as an assertion failure message. Defaults to /dev/termination-log. Cannot be updated.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#termination_message_path PodV1#termination_message_path}

---

##### `termination_message_policy`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="termination_message_policy" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecInitContainer.property.terminationMessagePolicy"></a>

```python
termination_message_policy: str
```

- *Type:* str

Optional: Indicate how the termination message should be populated.

File will use the contents of terminationMessagePath to populate the container status message on both success and failure. FallbackToLogsOnError will use the last chunk of container log output if the termination message file is empty and the container exited with an error. The log output is limited to 2048 bytes or 80 lines, whichever is smaller. Defaults to File. Cannot be updated.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#termination_message_policy PodV1#termination_message_policy}

### PodV1SpecInitContainerLifecyclePostStartExec <a name="PodV1SpecInitContainerLifecyclePostStartExec" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecInitContainerLifecyclePostStartExec"></a>

#### Initializer <a name="Initializer" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecInitContainerLifecyclePostStartExec.Initializer"></a>

```python
from cdktn_provider_kubernetes import pod_v1

podV1.PodV1SpecInitContainerLifecyclePostStartExec(
  command: typing.List[str] = None
)
```

#### Properties <a name="Properties" id="Properties"></a>

| **Name** | **Type** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <code><a href="#@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecInitContainerLifecyclePostStartExec.property.command">command</a></code> | <code>typing.List[str]</code> | Command is the command line to execute inside the container, the working directory for the command is root ('/') in the container's filesystem. |

---

##### `command`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="command" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecInitContainerLifecyclePostStartExec.property.command"></a>

```python
command: typing.List[str]
```

- *Type:* typing.List[str]

Command is the command line to execute inside the container, the working directory for the command is root ('/') in the container's filesystem.

The command is simply exec'd, it is not run inside a shell, so traditional shell instructions. To use a shell, you need to explicitly call out to that shell. Exit status of 0 is treated as live/healthy and non-zero is unhealthy.

Command is the command line to execute inside the container, the working directory for the command is root ('/') in the container's filesystem.

The command is simply exec'd, it is not run inside a shell, so traditional shell instructions. To use a shell, you need to explicitly call out to that shell. Exit status of 0 is treated as live/healthy and non-zero is unhealthy.


- *Type:* typing.List[str]

Command is the command line to execute inside the container, the working directory for the command is root ('/') in the container's filesystem.

The command is simply exec'd, it is not run inside a shell, so traditional shell instructions. To use a shell, you need to explicitly call out to that shell. Exit status of 0 is treated as live/healthy and non-zero is unhealthy.


- *Type:* typing.List[str]

Command is the command line to execute inside the container, the working directory for the command is root ('/') in the container's filesystem.

The command is simply exec'd, it is not run inside a shell, so traditional shell instructions. To use a shell, you need to explicitly call out to that shell. Exit status of 0 is treated as live/healthy and non-zero is unhealthy.

- *Type:* bool | cdktn.IResolvable

```python
run_as_non_root: bool | IResolvable
```

- *Type:* bool | cdktn.IResolvable

Indicates that the container must run as a non-root user.

If true, the Kubelet will validate the image at runtime to ensure that it does not run as UID 0 (root) and fail to start the container if it does. If unset or false, no such validation will be performed. May also be set in PodSecurityContext. If set in both SecurityContext and PodSecurityContext, the value specified in SecurityContext takes precedence.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#run_as_non_root PodV1#run_as_non_root}


Command is the command line to execute inside the container, the working directory for the command is root ('/') in the container's filesystem.

The command is simply exec'd, it is not run inside a shell, so traditional shell instructions. To use a shell, you need to explicitly call out to that shell. Exit status of 0 is treated as live/healthy and non-zero is unhealthy.

---

##### `fs_group`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="fs_group" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecSecurityContext.property.fsGroup"></a>

```python
fs_group: str
```

- *Type:* str

A special supplemental group that applies to all containers in a pod.

Some volume types allow the Kubelet to change the ownership of that volume to be owned by the pod: 1. The owning GID will be the FSGroup 2. The setgid bit is set (new files created in the volume will be owned by FSGroup) 3. The permission bits are OR'd with rw-rw---- If unset, the Kubelet will not modify the ownership and permissions of any volume.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#fs_group PodV1#fs_group}

---

##### `fs_group_change_policy`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="fs_group_change_policy" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecSecurityContext.property.fsGroupChangePolicy"></a>

```python
fs_group_change_policy: str
```

- *Type:* str

fsGroupChangePolicy defines behavior of changing ownership and permission of the volume before being exposed inside Pod.

This field will only apply to volume types which support fsGroup based ownership(and permissions). It will have no effect on ephemeral volume types such as: secret, configmaps and emptydir.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#fs_group_change_policy PodV1#fs_group_change_policy}

---

##### `run_as_group`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="run_as_group" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecSecurityContext.property.runAsGroup"></a>

```python
run_as_group: str
```

- *Type:* str

The GID to run the entrypoint of the container process.

Uses runtime default if unset. May also be set in SecurityContext. If set in both SecurityContext and PodSecurityContext, the value specified in SecurityContext takes precedence for that container.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#run_as_group PodV1#run_as_group}

---

##### `run_as_non_root`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="run_as_non_root" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecSecurityContext.property.runAsNonRoot"></a>

```python
run_as_non_root: bool | IResolvable
```

- *Type:* bool | cdktn.IResolvable

Indicates that the container must run as a non-root user.

If true, the Kubelet will validate the image at runtime to ensure that it does not run as UID 0 (root) and fail to start the container if it does. If unset or false, no such validation will be performed. May also be set in SecurityContext. If set in both SecurityContext and PodSecurityContext, the value specified in SecurityContext takes precedence.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#run_as_non_root PodV1#run_as_non_root}

---

```python
run_as_user: str
```

- *Type:* str

The UID to run the entrypoint of the container process.

Defaults to user specified in image metadata if unspecified. May also be set in SecurityContext. If set in both SecurityContext and PodSecurityContext, the value specified in SecurityContext takes precedence for that container.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#run_as_user PodV1#run_as_user}

- *Type:* typing.List[typing.Union[int, float]]

```python
)
```

#### Properties <a name="Properties" id="Properties"></a>

| **Name** | **Type** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <code><a href="#@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecToleration.property.effect">effect</a></code> | <code>str</code> | Effect indicates the taint effect to match. |
| <code><a href="#@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecToleration.property.key">key</a></code> | <code>str</code> | Key is the taint key that the toleration applies to. |

---

##### `effect`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="effect" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecToleration.property.effect"></a>

```python
effect: str
```

- *Type:* str

Effect indicates the taint effect to match.

Empty means match all taint effects. When specified, allowed values are NoSchedule, PreferNoSchedule and NoExecute.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#effect PodV1#effect}

---

##### `key`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="key" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecToleration.property.key"></a>

```python
key: str
```

- *Type:* str

Key is the taint key that the toleration applies to.

Empty means match all taint keys. If the key is empty, operator must be Exists; this combination means to match all values and all keys.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#key PodV1#key}

---

##### `operator`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="operator" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecToleration.property.operator"></a>

```python
operator: str
```

- *Type:* str

Operator represents a key's relationship to the value.

Valid operators are Exists and Equal. Defaults to Equal. Exists is equivalent to wildcard for value, so that a pod can tolerate all taints of a particular category.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#operator PodV1#operator}

---

##### `toleration_seconds`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="toleration_seconds" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecToleration.property.tolerationSeconds"></a>

```python
toleration_seconds: str
```

- *Type:* str

TolerationSeconds represents the period of time the toleration (which must be of effect NoExecute, otherwise this field is ignored) tolerates the taint.

By default, it is not set, which means tolerate the taint forever (do not evict). Zero and negative values will be treated as 0 (evict immediately) by the system.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#toleration_seconds PodV1#toleration_seconds}

---

##### `value`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="value" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecToleration.property.value"></a>

```python
value: str
```

- *Type:* str

Value is the taint value the toleration matches to.

If the operator is Exists, the value should be empty, otherwise just a regular string.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#value PodV1#value}

---


Filesystem type of the volume that you want to mount.

Tip: Ensure that the filesystem type is supported by the host operating system. Examples: "ext4", "xfs", "ntfs". Implicitly inferred to be "ext4" if unspecified. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/volumes#awselasticblockstore


- *Type:* typing.Union[int, float]

The partition in the volume that you want to mount.

If omitted, the default is to mount by volume name. Examples: For volume /dev/sda1, you specify the partition as "1". Similarly, the volume partition for /dev/sda is "0" (or you can leave the property empty).

###### `command`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="command" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecContainerLifecyclePostStartOutputReference.putExec.parameter.command"></a>

- *Type:* typing.List[str]

Command is the command line to execute inside the container, the working directory for the command is root ('/') in the container's filesystem.

The command is simply exec'd, it is not run inside a shell, so traditional shell instructions. To use a shell, you need to explicitly call out to that shell. Exit status of 0 is treated as live/healthy and non-zero is unhealthy.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#command PodV1#command}

```python
) -> None
```

###### `command`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="command" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecContainerLifecyclePreStopOutputReference.putExec.parameter.command"></a>

- *Type:* typing.List[str]

Command is the command line to execute inside the container, the working directory for the command is root ('/') in the container's filesystem.

The command is simply exec'd, it is not run inside a shell, so traditional shell instructions. To use a shell, you need to explicitly call out to that shell. Exit status of 0 is treated as live/healthy and non-zero is unhealthy.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#command PodV1#command}

```python
) -> None
```

###### `command`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="command" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecContainerLivenessProbeOutputReference.putExec.parameter.command"></a>

- *Type:* typing.List[str]

Command is the command line to execute inside the container, the working directory for the command is root ('/') in the container's filesystem.

The command is simply exec'd, it is not run inside a shell, so traditional shell instructions. To use a shell, you need to explicitly call out to that shell. Exit status of 0 is treated as live/healthy and non-zero is unhealthy.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#command PodV1#command}

```python
  privileged: bool | IResolvable = None,
  read_only_root_filesystem: bool | IResolvable = None,
```

###### `allow_privilege_escalation`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="allow_privilege_escalation" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecContainerOutputReference.putSecurityContext.parameter.allowPrivilegeEscalation"></a>

- *Type:* bool | cdktn.IResolvable

AllowPrivilegeEscalation controls whether a process can gain more privileges than its parent process.

This bool directly controls if the no_new_privs flag will be set on the container process. AllowPrivilegeEscalation is true always when the container is: 1) run as Privileged 2) has CAP_SYS_ADMIN

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#allow_privilege_escalation PodV1#allow_privilege_escalation}

Processes in privileged containers are essentially equivalent to root on the host. Defaults to false.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#read_only_root_filesystem PodV1#read_only_root_filesystem}

###### `run_as_group`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="run_as_group" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecContainerOutputReference.putSecurityContext.parameter.runAsGroup"></a>

- *Type:* str

The GID to run the entrypoint of the container process.

Uses runtime default if unset. May also be set in PodSecurityContext. If set in both SecurityContext and PodSecurityContext, the value specified in SecurityContext takes precedence.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#run_as_group PodV1#run_as_group}

###### `run_as_non_root`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="run_as_non_root" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecContainerOutputReference.putSecurityContext.parameter.runAsNonRoot"></a>

- *Type:* bool | cdktn.IResolvable

Indicates that the container must run as a non-root user.

If true, the Kubelet will validate the image at runtime to ensure that it does not run as UID 0 (root) and fail to start the container if it does. If unset or false, no such validation will be performed. May also be set in PodSecurityContext. If set in both SecurityContext and PodSecurityContext, the value specified in SecurityContext takes precedence.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#run_as_non_root PodV1#run_as_non_root}

###### `command`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="command" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecContainerReadinessProbeOutputReference.putExec.parameter.command"></a>

- *Type:* typing.List[str]

Command is the command line to execute inside the container, the working directory for the command is root ('/') in the container's filesystem.

The command is simply exec'd, it is not run inside a shell, so traditional shell instructions. To use a shell, you need to explicitly call out to that shell. Exit status of 0 is treated as live/healthy and non-zero is unhealthy.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#command PodV1#command}

##### `put_exec` <a name="put_exec" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecContainerStartupProbeOutputReference.putExec"></a>

```python
def put_exec(
  command: typing.List[str] = None
) -> None
```

###### `command`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="command" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecContainerStartupProbeOutputReference.putExec.parameter.command"></a>

- *Type:* typing.List[str]

Command is the command line to execute inside the container, the working directory for the command is root ('/') in the container's filesystem.

The command is simply exec'd, it is not run inside a shell, so traditional shell instructions. To use a shell, you need to explicitly call out to that shell. Exit status of 0 is treated as live/healthy and non-zero is unhealthy.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#command PodV1#command}

###### `command`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="command" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecInitContainerLifecyclePostStartOutputReference.putExec.parameter.command"></a>

- *Type:* typing.List[str]

Command is the command line to execute inside the container, the working directory for the command is root ('/') in the container's filesystem.

The command is simply exec'd, it is not run inside a shell, so traditional shell instructions. To use a shell, you need to explicitly call out to that shell. Exit status of 0 is treated as live/healthy and non-zero is unhealthy.

```python
) -> None
```

###### `command`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="command" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecInitContainerLifecyclePreStopOutputReference.putExec.parameter.command"></a>

- *Type:* typing.List[str]

Command is the command line to execute inside the container, the working directory for the command is root ('/') in the container's filesystem.

The command is simply exec'd, it is not run inside a shell, so traditional shell instructions. To use a shell, you need to explicitly call out to that shell. Exit status of 0 is treated as live/healthy and non-zero is unhealthy.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#command PodV1#command}

```python
) -> None
```

###### `command`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="command" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecInitContainerLivenessProbeOutputReference.putExec.parameter.command"></a>

- *Type:* typing.List[str]

Command is the command line to execute inside the container, the working directory for the command is root ('/') in the container's filesystem.

The command is simply exec'd, it is not run inside a shell, so traditional shell instructions. To use a shell, you need to explicitly call out to that shell. Exit status of 0 is treated as live/healthy and non-zero is unhealthy.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#command PodV1#command}

###### `allow_privilege_escalation`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="allow_privilege_escalation" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecInitContainerOutputReference.putSecurityContext.parameter.allowPrivilegeEscalation"></a>

- *Type:* bool | cdktn.IResolvable

AllowPrivilegeEscalation controls whether a process can gain more privileges than its parent process.

This bool directly controls if the no_new_privs flag will be set on the container process. AllowPrivilegeEscalation is true always when the container is: 1) run as Privileged 2) has CAP_SYS_ADMIN

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#allow_privilege_escalation PodV1#allow_privilege_escalation}

###### `run_as_group`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="run_as_group" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecInitContainerOutputReference.putSecurityContext.parameter.runAsGroup"></a>

- *Type:* str

The GID to run the entrypoint of the container process.

Uses runtime default if unset. May also be set in PodSecurityContext. If set in both SecurityContext and PodSecurityContext, the value specified in SecurityContext takes precedence.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#run_as_group PodV1#run_as_group}

###### `run_as_non_root`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="run_as_non_root" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecInitContainerOutputReference.putSecurityContext.parameter.runAsNonRoot"></a>

- *Type:* bool | cdktn.IResolvable

Indicates that the container must run as a non-root user.

If true, the Kubelet will validate the image at runtime to ensure that it does not run as UID 0 (root) and fail to start the container if it does. If unset or false, no such validation will be performed. May also be set in PodSecurityContext. If set in both SecurityContext and PodSecurityContext, the value specified in SecurityContext takes precedence.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#run_as_non_root PodV1#run_as_non_root}

##### `put_exec` <a name="put_exec" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecInitContainerReadinessProbeOutputReference.putExec"></a>

```python
def put_exec(
  command: typing.List[str] = None
) -> None
```

###### `command`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="command" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecInitContainerReadinessProbeOutputReference.putExec.parameter.command"></a>

- *Type:* typing.List[str]

Command is the command line to execute inside the container, the working directory for the command is root ('/') in the container's filesystem.

The command is simply exec'd, it is not run inside a shell, so traditional shell instructions. To use a shell, you need to explicitly call out to that shell. Exit status of 0 is treated as live/healthy and non-zero is unhealthy.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#command PodV1#command}

```python
) -> None
```

###### `command`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="command" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecInitContainerStartupProbeOutputReference.putExec.parameter.command"></a>

- *Type:* typing.List[str]

Command is the command line to execute inside the container, the working directory for the command is root ('/') in the container's filesystem.

The command is simply exec'd, it is not run inside a shell, so traditional shell instructions. To use a shell, you need to explicitly call out to that shell. Exit status of 0 is treated as live/healthy and non-zero is unhealthy.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#command PodV1#command}

##### `put_security_context` <a name="put_security_context" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecOutputReference.putSecurityContext"></a>

```python
def put_security_context(
  fs_group: str = None,
  fs_group_change_policy: str = None,
  run_as_group: str = None,
  run_as_non_root: bool | IResolvable = None,
  run_as_user: str = None,
  seccomp_profile: PodV1SpecSecurityContextSeccompProfile = None,
  se_linux_options: PodV1SpecSecurityContextSeLinuxOptions = None,
  supplemental_groups: typing.List[typing.Union[int, float]] = None,
  sysctl: IResolvable | typing.List[PodV1SpecSecurityContextSysctl] = None,
  windows_options: PodV1SpecSecurityContextWindowsOptions = None
) -> None
```

###### `fs_group`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="fs_group" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecOutputReference.putSecurityContext.parameter.fsGroup"></a>

- *Type:* str

A special supplemental group that applies to all containers in a pod.

Some volume types allow the Kubelet to change the ownership of that volume to be owned by the pod: 1. The owning GID will be the FSGroup 2. The setgid bit is set (new files created in the volume will be owned by FSGroup) 3. The permission bits are OR'd with rw-rw---- If unset, the Kubelet will not modify the ownership and permissions of any volume.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#fs_group PodV1#fs_group}

---

###### `fs_group_change_policy`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="fs_group_change_policy" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecOutputReference.putSecurityContext.parameter.fsGroupChangePolicy"></a>

- *Type:* str

fsGroupChangePolicy defines behavior of changing ownership and permission of the volume before being exposed inside Pod.

This field will only apply to volume types which support fsGroup based ownership(and permissions). It will have no effect on ephemeral volume types such as: secret, configmaps and emptydir.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#fs_group_change_policy PodV1#fs_group_change_policy}

---

###### `run_as_group`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="run_as_group" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecOutputReference.putSecurityContext.parameter.runAsGroup"></a>

- *Type:* str

The GID to run the entrypoint of the container process.

Uses runtime default if unset. May also be set in SecurityContext. If set in both SecurityContext and PodSecurityContext, the value specified in SecurityContext takes precedence for that container.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#run_as_group PodV1#run_as_group}

---

###### `run_as_non_root`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="run_as_non_root" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecOutputReference.putSecurityContext.parameter.runAsNonRoot"></a>

- *Type:* bool | cdktn.IResolvable

Indicates that the container must run as a non-root user.

If true, the Kubelet will validate the image at runtime to ensure that it does not run as UID 0 (root) and fail to start the container if it does. If unset or false, no such validation will be performed. May also be set in SecurityContext. If set in both SecurityContext and PodSecurityContext, the value specified in SecurityContext takes precedence.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#run_as_non_root PodV1#run_as_non_root}

---

###### `run_as_user`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="run_as_user" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecOutputReference.putSecurityContext.parameter.runAsUser"></a>

- *Type:* str

The UID to run the entrypoint of the container process.

Defaults to user specified in image metadata if unspecified. May also be set in SecurityContext. If set in both SecurityContext and PodSecurityContext, the value specified in SecurityContext takes precedence for that container.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#run_as_user PodV1#run_as_user}

---

###### `seccomp_profile`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="seccomp_profile" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecOutputReference.putSecurityContext.parameter.seccompProfile"></a>

- *Type:* <a href="#@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecSecurityContextSeccompProfile">PodV1SpecSecurityContextSeccompProfile</a>

seccomp_profile block.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#seccomp_profile PodV1#seccomp_profile}

Filesystem type of the volume that you want to mount.

Tip: Ensure that the filesystem type is supported by the host operating system. Examples: "ext4", "xfs", "ntfs". Implicitly inferred to be "ext4" if unspecified. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/volumes#awselasticblockstore

If omitted, the default is to mount by volume name. Examples: For volume /dev/sda1, you specify the partition as "1". Similarly, the volume partition for /dev/sda is "0" (or you can leave the property empty).

###### `default_mode`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="default_mode" id="@cdktn/provider-kubernetes.podV1.PodV1SpecVolumeOutputReference.putSecret.parameter.defaultMode"></a>

- *Type:* str

Optional: mode bits to use on created files by default.

Must be a value between 0 and 0777. Defaults to 0644. Directories within the path are not affected by this setting. This might be in conflict with other options that affect the file mode, like fsGroup, and the result can be other mode bits set.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/kubernetes/2.38.0/docs/resources/pod_v1#default_mode PodV1#default_mode}
